title: P2P-Chiplet: Partition and Placement Co-Optimization for Multi-Chiplet Architecture
problem: Multi-chiplet designs require optimizing partition (block-to-die assignment) and placement sequentially, but this dependency creates partition-placement inconsistency where solutions optimal in one phase may yield inferior overall results. Existing frameworks fail to harness co-optimization benefits.
motivation: Modern cost pressures prevent large monolithic SoCs from following Moore's Law, requiring multi-chiplet designs where partition and placement decisions must be jointly optimized to realize the full benefit of chiplet disaggregation.
method: Introduces HeteroACG, an optimized Abstract Constraint Graph structure that aggregates topological partition and physical placement optimization spaces. Decomposes sequential partition-placement flow into interleaved fine-grained epochs and employs alternating progressive optimization strategy to maintain partition-placement consistency. Uses progressive epoch updates to refine solutions iteratively.
key_novelty: First partition-placement co-optimization framework addressing the partition-placement inconsistency problem through interleaved fine-grained epochs and HeteroACG structure.
contributions: HeteroACG structure enabling unified optimization of partition and placement decisions
Alternating progressive optimization strategy preserving partition-placement consistency
Demonstrates cost reduction and performance improvement over sequential approaches
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific chiplet configurations; scalability to very large numbers of chiplets not clearly demonstrated; overhead of interleaved epochs not fully characterized.
